agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: Among the full-attention layers, only layer 11 reads the last prompt token. Head 3 puts 25–27% of its attention there, head 2 even more (22–33%), and head 0 10–12%. Layers 5, 17 and 23 stay below 5%. Layer 11 has a single shared key/value head, so heads 0 and 2 read the same constant value v_t and write it through their own o_proj columns. They are natural next candidates for the same rank-1 removal. First I'll run E13 (head 3 rank-1 removal only, no E4) to learn whether the neuron edit adds anything once head 3's constant read is gone. A result close to +27 would mean E4 is redundant, and I'd drop it to keep the edit minimal.

E13, the rank-1 removal in head 3 alone with no neuron edit, gains +28.5 ± 3.3 (83 wrong→right, 10 right→wrong; 47.3% against 18.75%). E4 is redundant once head 3 no longer reads the constant last-prompt value, consistent with head 3 being upstream of 6176/6508. E13 is now my best candidate, a single rank-1 change, and I'll save it as /work/best_4. Next I'll test whether the same constant read through heads 0 and 2 also suppresses. They share the KV head and attend to the last prompt token at 10–33%. E14 applies the same rank-1 removal of v̂ to the o_proj columns of heads 0, 2 and 3. A gain clearly above E13's would extend the mechanism to the whole layer-11 read of the prompt summary. A drop would mean those heads' copies are useful, and E13 stays.
E14 is saved: the rank-1 removal of v̂ is now applied to heads 0, 2 and 3 of layer 11. I'll run the paired generation on dev_b[:256] and compare it with E13's +28.5.

E14, the rank-1 removal in heads 0, 2 and 3, gains +31.6 ± 3.4 (92 wrong→right, 11 right→wrong; 50.4% against 18.75%), against +28.5 for head 3 alone on the same problems. The difference of about 3 points is within noise, but it goes the expected way: heads 0 and 2 read the same constant value through the shared KV head. Strength and head choices have all been tuned on dev_b[:256], so before freezing I'll replicate E14 on fresh DEV problems, dev_a[:256], which no edit has been tuned on. A gain of similar size there (+25 to +30) would show the effect is not an artifact of repeated use of one set, and I'd freeze E14 for HOLDOUT. A much smaller gain would mean I've overfit the choices and should reconsider.
